title: Holomorphic dependence of a circle Cauchy integral on complex parameters
statement:
Work over $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $d\geq0$, let $P\subset\mathbf C^d$ be open, let $c\in\mathbf C$, and let $R>0$ and $0<\epsilon<R$. Put $A=\{\zeta\in\mathbf C:R-\epsilon<|\zeta-c|<R+\epsilon\}$ and $D=\{z\in\mathbf C:|z-c|<R\}$. Let $g:A\times P\to\mathbf C$ be holomorphic, meaning locally represented by a convergent complex power series in all $d+1$ coordinates. For $(z,w)\in D\times P$ the positively oriented circle integral
$$H(z,w)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{|\zeta-c|=R}\frac{g(\zeta,w)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta$$
exists and defines a holomorphic function $H:D\times P\to\mathbf C$ in the same power-series sense. The circle is parametrized by $\zeta=c+Re^{it}$ for $0\leq t\leq2\pi$.

source.place: I §3.B, formulas (3.8)--(3.9), printed p.22, parameter-integral consequence of the uniform Cauchy expansions, with I §3.A (3.3), printed p.21. This consequence is formulated by the worker, not a separately numbered theorem. WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Fix $(z_0,w_0)\in D\times P$; if $P=\varnothing$ there is nothing to prove. Put $K=\{|\zeta-c|=R\}\subset A$, $\delta=R-|z_0-c|>0$, and choose $0<r<\delta$ and $0<\rho<s$ with the closed parameter polydisc $Q_s$ about $w_0$ contained in $P$. Holomorphy implies continuity by [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]; since $|\zeta-z|\geq R-|z-c|>0$ on $K$, the parametrized integrand is continuous and its integral exists. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-parameter-taylor-expansion] to $U=A$, this compact $K$, $w_0,s$. It gives continuous $a_\alpha$ and $M$ with $g(\zeta,w_0+v)=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha(\zeta)v^\alpha$ and $|a_\alpha(\zeta)|\leq Ms^{-|\alpha|}$, uniformly on $K\times Q_\rho$.

source.place: I §3.A (3.3), I §3.B (3.8)–(3.9), worker-written parameter-integral assembly; local PDF missing.

proof.text:
For $|u|\leq r$ and $\zeta\in K$, $|\zeta-z_0|\geq\delta$. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-geometric-series] with $q=u/(\zeta-z_0)$ and multiply by $(\zeta-z_0)^{-1}$. This gives the kernel expansion
$$\frac1{\zeta-z_0-u}=\sum_{n\geq0}\frac{u^n}{(\zeta-z_0)^{n+1}}.$$
Its terms have absolute value at most $\delta^{-1}(r/\delta)^n$; its tail from $n=N$ is at most $\delta^{-1}(r/\delta)^N/(1-r/\delta)$, independently of $\zeta,u$. Thus convergence is absolute and uniform on the stated sets.

source.place: I §3.A (3.3), I §3.B (3.8)–(3.9), worker-written parameter-integral assembly; local PDF missing.

proof.text:
Put $p=r/\delta<1$ and $q=\rho/s<1$. The product terms $a_\alpha(\zeta)u^nv^\alpha/(\zeta-z_0)^{n+1}$ are bounded by $M\delta^{-1}p^nq^{|\alpha|}$. On the box $n<N$, $\alpha_j<N$, the sum of these majorants is
$$\frac M\delta\Bigl(\sum_{n<N}p^n\Bigr)\prod_{j=1}^d\Bigl(\sum_{k<N}q^k\Bigr)\ \longrightarrow\ \frac{M}{\delta(1-p)(1-q)^d}$$
by [lem-sfb-scalar-geometric-series]. The sum outside the box is bounded by this last constant times $p^N+dq^N$ (union over the coordinates outside the box), which tends to zero. Every finite subset of $\mathbf N\times\mathbf N^d$ is contained in a box. These bounds prove absolute uniform convergence of the double series and identify its sum with the product of the two expansions by multiplying the finite rectangular sums and taking their limits. Since the majorant family $M\delta^{-1}p^nq^{|\alpha|}$ is summable over $\mathbf N\times\mathbf N^d$ (its finite subsums are bounded by $M/[\delta(1-p)(1-q)^d]$), [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] with $I=\mathbf N\times\mathbf N^d$ shows that the complex product terms, their supremum norms, and any family bounded by these majorants are summable.

source.place: I §3.A (3.3), I §3.B (3.8)–(3.9), worker-written parameter-integral assembly; local PDF missing.

proof.text:
Write $\gamma(t)=c+Re^{it}$, so $|\gamma'(t)|=R$. The functions
$$f_{n,\alpha}(t)=\frac{a_\alpha(\gamma(t))u^nv^\alpha\gamma'(t)}{(\gamma(t)-z_0)^{n+1}}$$
are continuous on $\mathbf R$ and their supremum norms on $[0,2\pi]$ are summable by step 3, with the additional factor $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-series-interval-integration] with $J=\mathbf N\times\mathbf N^d$: termwise integration gives
$$H(z_0+u,w_0+v)=\sum_{n,\alpha}b_{n,\alpha}u^nv^\alpha,\qquad b_{n,\alpha}=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{a_\alpha(\gamma(t))\gamma'(t)}{(\gamma(t)-z_0)^{n+1}}\,dt.$$
The bound clause of the same node gives $|b_{n,\alpha}|\leq RM\delta^{-n-1}s^{-|\alpha|}$. Consequently, by [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] and the majorant of step 3, the coefficient series on $|u|\leq r$, $|v_j|\leq\rho$ is absolutely convergent, bounded by $RM/[\delta(1-p)(1-q)^d]$. It is the required convergent power series in all $d+1$ coordinates. Since the point was arbitrary, this is exactly holomorphy as defined in the item; no gluing theorem is needed.
